profile.owner: EverCommerce (Nasdaq: EVCM), which acquired Briostack in January 2021; sold under the EverPro home and field services brand. Founded by Brandon Grover; based in Lehi, Utah. EverCommerce bought AI agent company ZyraTalk in September 2025 and announced a CEO transition in August 2026.
profile.target_customers: Small and mid-sized residential and commercial pest control companies in North America, plus lawn care and mixed pest and lawn operators. Claims 3,700+ pest professionals as users. Capterra reviewers mostly have 2 to 50 employees. Strong fit for companies running door-to-door sales teams.
profile.pricing: Not published by the vendor: custom quotes with concurrent licensing by active users rather than total seats. Figures from a third-party demo report ($95 per month per office user, $45 per month per technician, $250 training fee, Playbooks marketing add-on $299 per month list) could not be re-verified because that page now returns 404. Terms (updated October 2025): one-year initial term from go-live that auto-renews, 30 days' notice to end, non-refundable fees and an early termination fee equal to the monthly fees for the remaining months. Published add-on fees include SMS $0.04 per text, calls $0.04 per minute, an $11 10DLC fee, $250 per additional import, $150 per custom document and $500 per database backup. Capterra lists a starting price of $50 per month (Basic). Public API Basic and Premium tiers are by quote.
profile.deployment: Cloud, browser-based web app for office staff (admin work is web only), with native iOS and Android technician app.
profile.mobile_app: Brio Tech (iOS and Android; technician app with claimed offline support, also used for field sales and bids; version 1.4.2 released October 2026) plus Brio Sales 2 for door-to-door reps. The US App Store showed no Brio Tech ratings on 2026-10-29; a third-party review cites 2.0 from 5 ratings. Modules are branded Brio Office (web), Brio Tech (field) and Brio Sales (sales).
integrations: CardConnect and Clover Connect payment processing (Fiserv)
Voice For Pest and Voice for Turf phone systems
Swell (review requests, two-way inbox, NPS surveys)
Customer Lobby Prospect Marketing direct mail (EverPro)
strengths: Mature scheduling and routing: cadence-based auto scheduling, seasonal templates, unlimited route optimization, bulk reschedule and multi-branch views.
Offline-capable technician app with product application capture, photos, notes, barcode scanning and field payments.
Built-in sales tooling: territories, sales maps, leaderboards, commission plans, pricing calculator and satellite-image bid diagrams.
Many reviewers praise onboarding, data migration and responsive support reps.
EverCommerce backing adds an ecosystem of add-ons (AI answering, direct mail, Swell) and a public API.
weaknesses: Frequent reports of glitches, crashes and new bugs after updates, including some lost data.
Contract and billing complaints: annual non-refundable terms, early termination fees, undisclosed add-on charges and SMS price increases.
Reports can be hard to find; termite graphing, bundles and skills-based routing are requested gaps; some dislike route results.
Support quality is inconsistent in negative reviews (slow replies, unreturned calls), and admin controls are limited.

No built-in general ledger (relies on QuickBooks Online); per-user pricing was a reviewer complaint, though the vendor now sells concurrent licenses by active users; seen as more pest-focused than lawn.

features.notes: Leads managed in web and field apps, with sales funnel insights on dashboards. Defined pipeline stages are not publicly documented.
No public mention of lead source fields or close rate by source reporting.
Bids with preset bid types, square foot or flat rate pricing calculator, photos and diagrams. Tiered good, better, best options not shown.
Vendor lists e-signatures among paperless tools, and customers respond to proposals in the portal. Exact agreement signing flow not publicly documented.
Sales app supports field sign-ups, territory assignments, partitioned sales maps and leaderboards. Knock tracking is not documented.
Custom commission plans with automated calculations and payout tracking. Holds or chargebacks on early cancellation not documented.
Playbooks marketing add-on (Growth Bundle) supplies email and text campaign templates and reporting; a third-party demo reported $299 per month list, but that page now returns 404.
Dashboards track attrition rate and win-back messages target cancelled customers. Cancellation reason codes and save workflows not documented.
Multi-unit commercial module offers billing options for multi-unit buildings and large corporate accounts. One reviewer reported apartment unit-level gaps.
Phone integration through partner Voice For Pest (Voice for Turf for lawn); native click to call or caller ID pop not documented.
Automated appointments from set service cadences, including twice-monthly by week and day, with service templates holding prices.

Seasonal appointment templates space each service type by a number of days. A fixed number of rounds inside a date window is not described for pest (the lawn page describes rounds), so this Yes is weak.

Pricing calculator by square foot or flat rate standardizes bids, and a vendor comparison page now claims service bundles that reviewers had reported missing; a central add-on price book is not documented.
Bulk price changes by segment or service with customer notification. A reviewer notes it only tracks increases made through that tool.
Renewal notices exist, but term length, auto-renewal and early cancellation fee tracking per agreement are not publicly documented.
Termite and bed bug warranties with start dates and automated renewal notifications for expiring warranties.
A third-party demo noted a reservice rate report, but that page returned 404 on 2026-10-29 and no vendor page mentions re-service; logging free return visits with cost is not documented.
Visits generated automatically from preset service cadences and multi-visit service timelines.
Calendar and map views filterable by branch, tech and color-coded category; drag and drop is listed by review sites.
Route optimization with automatic recalculation, marketed as unlimited at no extra cost. Some reviewers dislike the resulting routes.
Automatic best-fit tech recommendations exist, but skill or license criteria are not documented and reviewers request skills-based routing.
Portal covers billing, payments, proposals and notification preferences; customer self-booking or rescheduling is not clearly documented.
Built-in GPS technician tracking plus Azuga fleet telematics partner. A third-party demo said GPS is not real time.
Bulk rescheduling by tech or branch, plus a bulk mover between techs and branches.
Brio Tech app for iOS and Android (version 1.4.2, October 2026), used for routes, jobs, chemical reporting and payments; door-to-door reps also have the separate Brio Sales 2 app.

Scheduling page says tech app tools work with or without data connectivity and a comparison table checks offline mode, but the product FAQ says all you need is an internet connection; offline depth is undocumented.
Technicians record product applications and chemical usage on the visit from the app.
App supports photos on appointments and services plus notes; signature capture is cited on vendor and review listings.
Barcode scanning tracks equipment placed on job sites and reports on each site.
App listing confirms collecting payments in the field.
No public mention of a technician time clock; geotracking check-ins exist but hours for payroll are not documented.
No public documentation of vehicle stock being visible or editable on the device.
Pesticide logs and chemical usage reports are captured per visit and pitched for inspection readiness; state-specific record formats are not documented.

Vendor comparison pages cite chemical and product application tracking; EPA numbers, label and SDS storage are not documented. Custom chemical lists reported by a third-party demo could not be re-verified (page now returns 404).
A vendor comparison page (October 2026) lists technician licensing and product controls with no detail; license numbers, categories and expiry alerts are not documented.

A vendor comparison page (October 2026) claims built-in state-specific WDI/WDO forms for all 50 states and a direct California Department of Agriculture integration, without feature documentation; no other state pesticide report formats are named.
Automated appointment reminders exist, but pesticide pre or post application notices are not documented.
No RUP record fields or controls documented; a vendor comparison page lists technician licensing and product controls with no detail.
Vendor FAQ claims inventory management features; warehouse, purchasing and transfer depth is not publicly documented.

Claims state-specific WDI/WDO forms for all 50 states and a California Department of Agriculture integration (October 2026 comparison page), without documentation; no state notice or registry rules found.
Barcode tracking of equipment placed on job sites; reviewers track bait station activity, though one says stations are entered one by one.
Satellite-image diagrams with bait station annotations; interior floor plan device maps are not documented.
Pest activity tracking at each job site is documented; per-device trend reports over time are not described.
No mention of AIB, SQF, BRC or other audit-ready documentation.
Customer portal shows service and billing history; commercial access to maps, labels and SDS is not documented.
No public documentation of customer sighting logs or corrective action tracking.
Multi-unit commercial module adds specialized billing options for large accounts; PO numbers and net terms are not documented.

Satellite diagramming marketed as termite graph software, bait station annotations and termite warranties; a vendor comparison page now claims state-specific WDI/WDO forms for all 50 states and a Sentricon integration, without documentation. Reviewers want better graphing.
No wildlife trapping, exclusion or repair job features found.
Preset multi-visit service schedules are cited for bed bugs, plus bed bug warranties; customer prep checklists are not documented.
No mosquito or tick specific features named; generic seasonal appointment templates could cover seasonal programs.
Built-in payment processing through CardConnect or Clover Connect (Fiserv backend), with rate matching offered. ACH support not publicly confirmed.
Portal lets customers update billing information and automated card charging is cited; a third-party demo confirmed autopay.
Flexible payment models including monthly or production-based subscriptions and prepayment campaigns.
No public documentation of tax rates by service address or per-service taxability.
Automated billing reminders, late notices and mailed collection letters; payment retries, late fees and service holds are not documented.
Consolidated statements not documented; a reviewer requested a total outstanding balance view across accounts.
No public documentation of proration or balance due when an agreement is cancelled.
No general ledger; vendor positions QuickBooks Online as the accounting system and pushes transactions there. Receivables are handled in product.
Integrates with QuickBooks Online, including QuickBooks Online Advanced per GetApp. QuickBooks Desktop support not mentioned.
No Sage, Xero, NetSuite or other accounting integrations found; the public API could support custom connections.
Prepayment campaigns exist, but deferred revenue recognition as visits are performed is not documented.
Campaign profitability and operational cost reports mentioned; per-job labor and material costing with margin is not documented.
Payroll and production reports are listed; payroll provider integration and production pay rules are not documented.
24/7 portal for billing details, online payments, service records, notification preferences and proposal responses.
Automated text, call and email appointment reminders are documented; technician en route notices are not.
Centralized two-way client inbox came through the Swell integration (announced 2022); native two-way texting is not documented.
Google review request texts via the Swell integration; natively, the portal lets customers rate technicians after jobs.
Tech app generates documents and records products, but automatic service reports to customers listing products are not confirmed.
Dashboards and reports for revenue trends and forecasts, accounts receivable, payroll and production.
Attrition rate on dashboards and a cancellations report, and Brio Insights dashboards (Growth Bundle) track cancellations; breakdowns by route, technician or service are not documented.

Production and payroll reports exist; a reservice rate report was reported only by a third-party demo whose page now returns 404, and time on site and per-technician productivity detail are not documented.
Review sites list customizable reports and the public API exposes data; no documented report builder, and reviewers say reports are hard to find.
Multiple branches and work units with branch filters, bulk moves between branches and multi-location receivables.
Role configuration is not documented; reviewers cite limited admin controls that require support for changes.
Public API with sandbox docs; free tier of 350 requests per month, paid Basic and Premium tiers. Webhooks and Zapier not mentioned.

Onboarding includes data transfer and case studies cite migration. The published fee schedule charges $250 per additional import, $150 per non-standard data manipulation and $500 for Sentricon migration.

ZyraTalk AI answering service (EverPro) for inbound calls, priced by quote. A vendor page (October 2026) lists AI Note Refiner and Pest Identifier in preview and an AI Brio Assistant in development; Customer Lobby direct mail uses predictive AI targeting.
No hosted website or embeddable lead or booking forms found; marketing agency partner Socius Marketing is offered separately.
Customer Lobby prospect postcards via EverPro, Socius Marketing agency and Baton referrals are partner services; native click to mail letters also exist.

extra_features.feature: Satellite-image property diagramming with square footage calculation
extra_features.notes: Techs annotate high-resolution satellite images with treatment plans and bait stations, compute square footage and attach diagrams to bids.
Customizable company-wide or territory-specific leaderboards for sales reps, plus sales analytics.

extra_features.feature: Bid interest ranking and preset bid types
extra_features.notes: Bids are categorized by preset type and service category and ranked by customer interest level.
Send one text to all customers for weather delays or office closures.

extra_features.feature: Preferred contact channel routing including voice calls and mail
extra_features.notes: Reminders, invoices and quotes go out by each customer's preferred channel: email, text, recorded phone call or mail.

extra_features.feature: Click To Mail printed letters and postcards
extra_features.notes: Automated printed mail for renewal notices, collections and sales, sent from inside the product.
Techs can control their own schedule and route, reschedule with best-fit recommendations, and get turn-by-turn directions that re-optimize while driving.
Revenue forecasts and expected revenue by service based on scheduled work.
Run discount campaigns and track their profitability.

extra_features.feature: NPS surveys and internal team chat (Swell)
extra_features.notes: Swell integration adds private NPS survey texts and group or one-on-one chat among office, sales and technicians.
Partner network where companies refer vetted, exclusive leads to each other and pay only for matching referrals.
Free guided, step-by-step task help inside the product, plus a members-only community knowledge base and videos.
